summary.one_liner: Chipmunk is a native Rust desktop application for viewing log files of any size, collecting live logs from TCP, UDP, serial, or command output, and analyzing them with filters and regex-based charts.
summary.what_it_does: Opens log files of any size, limited only by disk space, and is described as avoiding unnecessary copying so large files open at the same speed. It collects logs over TCP, UDP, serial ports, or from the output of a running command, with a parser assignable to each source. It supports automotive trace formats such as DLT (including embedded attachments) and SomeIp, and can work with DLT inside pcap/pcapng captures. Users can create, save, and reuse filter sets with color labels, and search results update live as new data arrives. A graphing tool lets users define regular expressions to extract metrics and plot them in real time.
use_cases: collecting live logs from serial ports or network sockets
inspecting DLT or SomeIp content in pcap captures
filtering logs with saved, color-labeled filter sets
graphing metrics extracted from log lines
how_to_run: See the documentation for installation notes (the README does not give install or run commands).
notable: Handles log files of arbitrary size without copying them
Built-in DLT trace inspection, including embedded attachments
Live-updating search and regex-driven real-time charts
Can extract DLT content from SomeIp packets and pcap/pcapng captures
caveats: README does not state supported operating systems or installation steps; refers to external documentation
Automotive trace support (DLT, SomeIp) is the main focus, which may be less relevant for general logs
